findings.source_passage: Pip's blue, choked face plainly looked, Do, for God's sake! All passed in a flash. In less than half a minute, this entire thing happened.
findings.why_it_matters: The visual counterpoint—Pip's face silently begging 'Do, for God's sake!'—is rhetorically distinctive and dramatically essential, contrasting the spoken 'Cut?' with the unspoken plea. The speed markers ('All passed in a flash. In less than half a minute') are also rhythmically signature. The draft collapses this to a bare em-dash exchange.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Pip's blue, choked face plainly looked, Do, for God's sake! All passed in a flash.' after the 'Cut?'/'Damn him, cut!' exchange.

findings.source_passage: Stubb then in a plain, business-like, but still half humorous manner, cursed Pip officially; and that done, unofficially gave him much wholesome advice. The substance was, Never jump from a boat, Pip, except—but all the rest was indefinite, as the soundest advice ever is. Now, in general, Stick to the boat, is your true motto in whaling; but cases will sometimes happen when Leap from the boat, is still better.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after Pip is recovered, before Stubb's peremptory command
findings.why_it_matters: The ironic voice-establishment here—'all the rest was indefinite, as the soundest advice ever is'—and the mock-sententious 'Stick to the boat / Leap from the boat' dialectic are signature Melvillean comedy that frames the subsequent Alabama line. Erasing it collapses the rhetorical build-up.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'cursed Pip officially / unofficially' sequence and the 'Never jump from a boat, Pip, except—but all the rest was indefinite, as the soundest advice ever is' passage, including the italicized mottos.

findings.source_passage: It was a beautiful, bounteous, blue day; the spangled sea calm and cool, and flatly stretching away, all round, to the horizon, like gold-beater's skin hammered out to the extremest.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after Pip is left behind the second time
findings.why_it_matters: The alliterative 'beautiful, bounteous, blue' and 'calm and cool' with the full simile 'flatly stretching away, all round' carry prosodic distinctiveness. The draft reduces this to 'A bright, blue day; the spangled calm; the horizon hammered thin as gold-beater's skin,' losing 'bounteous,' 'cool,' and the rhythm of 'flatly stretching away, all round, to the horizon.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence: 'It was a beautiful, bounteous, blue day; the spangled sea calm and cool, and flatly stretching away, all round, to the horizon, like gold-beater's skin hammered out to the extremest.'

summary: The draft is largely faithful, preserving the major signatures including the 'God's foot upon the treadle of the loom,' 'man's insanity is heaven's sense,' and the castaway passage verbatim, but loses some voice-establishing ironic comedy around Stubb's advice and the silent dramatic detail of Pip's 'Do, for God's sake!' face.
